# Astro versioned documentation rehearsal

This draft is stacked on the unpublished Astro core-migration candidate. It does not change the released `/theme` lane. `docs-release-lock.json` pins the exact published core version and registry integrity used by the documentation build, independently of the Astro framework version. `scripts/docs-versions/build-release.mjs` packages the source candidate, installs Astro and core at exact direct versions into a disposable starter, captures the resulting npm lockfile, builds under the requested root or preview prefix, and emits a local noindex archive with a manifest and native version navigation. The immutable snapshot's static selector works without JavaScript; its archived navigation script can read a same-origin catalog to discover later versions while retaining the existing content and links if that catalog is unavailable. It never advances `latest`.

The caller must provide `DOCS_ARCHIVE_ROOT`, `DOCS_BASELINE_PATH`, `DOCS_BASELINE_SHA256` and `RELEASE_TAG`; the output directory and baseline are local rehearsal inputs. The shared snapshot code verifies previously recorded archives and core integrity, then reserves the new version without overwrite. It rejects an existing version. The baseline must come from independently authenticated, immutable storage in production. A caller-provided digest or local filesystem reservation alone cannot prevent someone from replacing both the baseline and archives remotely.

The starter is a five-page adoption specimen, not the complete reference site or the 50-example gallery. These tests do not establish full content parity, production hosting, manual screen-reader behavior, trusted catalog delivery, or immutable remote storage. Integration into tag publication must fail closed until a reviewed archive store, baseline authority, atomic create-only writes, retention, and independently controlled latest-pointer promotion and rollback are configured. No workflow here deploys a site or changes the current publication pipeline.
